newsitem.title: USA: Dow ends above 5,900 for first time as bonds rally.
newsitem.headline: Dow ends above 5,900 for first time as bonds rally.

text.p: The Dow industrials ended above 5,900 for the first time in history Tuesday and other stock indices shattered records on the first trading day of the fourth quarter, bolstered by a bond market rally.

"The market just keeps on trucking along. The pressure of (mutual fund) money is still there and as the day wore on, the strength in bonds transmitted to the equity market," said Marshall Acuff, portfolio strategist at Smith Barney.
The Dow Jones industrial average rose 22.73 to 5,904.90, topping the previous record closing high of 5,894.74 set on Sept. 23. That was also the day the Dow first ended above 5,800.

"It just puts us 100 points closer to 6,000. It's just a number. People are feeling a bit better. It gets back to the average guy on the street who's really making this happen with 401(K) and college fund contributions," said William LeFevre, a senior market analyst at Ehrenkrantz King Nussbaum.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,304 to 1,057 on heavy volume of 418.7 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
The Standard & Poor's index of 500 stocks rose 1.77 to a record 689.08, surpassing Monday's 687.33.
The NYSE Composite index set its fourth consecutive record, up 0.85 to 368.18. The average price per share rose 9 cents.
But the technology-studded Nasdaq Composite index lost 5.41 to 1,221.51, as earnings warnings from Xilinx Inc. and HCIA Inc. cast a pall on some high-technology stocks.
Stocks were bolstered by extended gains in the bond market, with the key 30-year Treasury bond surging 19/32 to yield 6.88 percent, down from 6.92 percent at Monday's close.

The National Association of Purchasing Management's September report showed moderate growth and no extreme price pressures. The NAPM index fell to 51.7 in September from 52.6 in August. Economists had forecast a reading of 52.5.
Separately, the Conference Board said its index of leading economic indicators rose 0.2 percent for August, in line with economists' forecasts.

Bond traders also noted rumours that an Australian financial newspaper quoted Australia's treasurer, who recently spoke to Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan, as saying Greenspan did not see U.S. inflation as a near-term problem.

"The bond market rallied, Greenspan made some positive comments and here we are," said Jim Pizzo, senior investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co. He noted Wall Street was still awaiting Friday's key employment report for September.
"Every (economic) report is heavily scrutinised. We have a lot of nervous people out there. And at these levels it's not in extremely strong hands," Pizzo said.

Among special situations, Xilinx, which supplies programmable logic devices to the phone and data networking industries, shed 2-3/8 to 31-5/8 after forecasting net income and revenue for the second quarter ended Sept. 28 would be below the first quarter's. UBS Securities cut the stock to hold from buy while other brokers slashed earnings estimates.
Micron Technology lost 1-3/8 to 29-1/8 amid chip sector weakness and news that Micron shuffled its board of directors.
Among other chip companies, Atmel lost 11/16 to 30-3/16, Altera eased 7/8 to 49-3/4 and Lattice Semi fell one to 27-7/8.

HFS Inc. surged 3-5/8 to 70-1/2 after news it is in talks to acquire a second unidentified rental car company this quarter. In August HFS said it reached a pact with General Motors Corp. to acquire its interest in Avis.

HCIA plummeted 45 percent or 27-1/8 points to 32-7/8 after warning weak revenues would drag its earnings well below expectations. Merrill downgraded the health care information company. Alex Brown cut HCIA to neutral from strong buy on the warning and then restored its strong buy on the stock drop.
The American Stock Exchange index fell 2.94 to 568.55.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was 6,773.184, up 7.535 points, or 0.11 percent.
